prompt: This command ran successfully on a freshly installed node. What happened?
explanation: `rladmin cluster join` is run on the new node itself and points at an existing cluster member — `nodes` takes the internal IP of a node already in the cluster, and the admin credentials are those of the cluster. Option B reverses the direction (you cannot push an install from the master), C describes `rladmin cluster create`, which bootstraps a new cluster, and D is what the `replace_node` flag of `cluster join` does, not a plain join.
code:
$ rladmin cluster join nodes 192.0.2.2 \
    username admin@example.com \
    password admin-password
Joining cluster... ok

options.text: A newly installed node joined the cluster that has a member at 192.0.2.2
The cluster master pushed the software installation out to 192.0.2.2
A brand-new cluster was bootstrapped with this node as its first member
This node replaced a failed node without losing the failed node's shards
